questions.questionText: Which cell organelle modifies, sorts, and packages newly synthesised glycoproteins into secretory vesicles?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus processes proteins arriving from the rough ER and buds off secretory vesicles.

questions.questionText: An organelle measures 12 mm across in an electron micrograph taken at magnification ×6,000. What is its actual diameter?
questions.explanation: Actual = Image / Magnification = 12 mm / 6,000 = 0.002 mm = 2.0 µm.

questions.questionText: Which bond links monosaccharides together to form maltose or starch during condensation reactions?
questions.explanation: Monosaccharides join via 1,4 or 1,6 glycosidic bonds eliminating H₂O.

questions.questionText: How does a competitive enzyme inhibitor reduce enzyme reaction rate?

options.text: Binds irreversibly to an allosteric site altering active site shape
Reversibly resembles substrate and competes directly for the active site (overcome at high [S])

questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors mimic the substrate and block the active site; V_max stays reachable at high [S].

questions.questionText: What happens to a red blood cell placed in a hypertonic concentrated sucrose solution?

options.text: It loses water by osmosis and becomes crenated (shrunken)
Nothing happens due to cellulose cell wall

questions.explanation: Water leaves down the water potential gradient causing crenation (plant cells plasmolyse).

questions.questionText: During which stage of the mitotic cell cycle does semi-conservative DNA replication occur?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes replicate into sister chromatids during S-phase before mitosis begins.

questions.questionText: If 22% of bases in a double-stranded DNA molecule are adenine (A), what percentage are cytosine (C)?
questions.explanation: By Chargaff's rule: A = T = 22% (sum 44%), leaving C + G = 56% -> C = 28%.

questions.questionText: Which RNA molecule carries a specific amino acid and matches its anticodon loop to the mRNA codon on a ribosome?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA (tRNA) bridges genetic triplet codons and specific amino acids during translation.

questions.questionText: What drives the upward mass flow of water and dissolved minerals in xylem vessels according to the cohesion-tension theory?

options.text: Transpiration pull from leaf mesophyll creating negative tension transmitted down cohesive water columns
Active ATP pumping by vessel walls

questions.explanation: Evaporation from leaves pulls continuous H-bonded water columns under tension up dead xylem vessels.

questions.questionText: What causes the Bohr shift in the haemoglobin oxygen dissociation curve during vigorous exercise?

options.text: Increased CO₂ / H⁺ acidity lowering haemoglobin affinity for O₂ so more O₂ unloads to active muscles

questions.explanation: Respiring tissues release CO₂ forming carbonic acid (H⁺), shifting the dissociation curve right to enhance O₂ unloading.

questions.questionText: Which immune cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete specific antibodies against a foreign antigen?
questions.explanation: Activated B-lymphocytes undergo clonal expansion into antibody-secreting plasma cells and memory B cells.

questions.questionText: In the kidney nephron, where does ultrafiltration of blood plasma occur under high hydrostatic pressure?
questions.explanation: Wider afferent than efferent arteriole creates high pressure forcing small solutes across podocytes into Bowman's capsule.

questions.questionText: Which ion rushes INTO the axon through voltage-gated channels to trigger depolarisation (+40 mV) during an action potential?
questions.explanation: Opening voltage-gated Na⁺ channels drives rapid Na⁺ influx, reversing membrane polarity.

questions.questionText: In the light-independent stage (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis, which 5-carbon acceptor molecule combines with CO₂ via Rubisco?
questions.explanation: Rubisco fixes CO₂ onto RuBP forming two 3-carbon GP molecules.

questions.questionText: In aerobic cellular respiration, what is the role of oxygen at the end of the mitochondrial electron transport chain?

options.text: Acts as the final electron and proton acceptor forming water
Pumps NADH out of the cell

questions.explanation: Oxygen accepts low-energy electrons and protons (½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O), keeping the ETC flowing.

questions.questionText: Two heterozygous plants (TtRr × TtRr) showing independent assortment are crossed. What phenotypic ratio is expected in the F₂ generation?
questions.explanation: Dihybrid cross between double heterozygotes yields classic Mendelian 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio.

questions.questionText: What is "allopatric speciation"?

options.text: Evolution of new species after populations are physically isolated by a geographic barrier
Formation of a new species without any geographic separation
A single base substitution in mRNA

questions.explanation: Physical barriers (rivers, mountains) halt gene flow, letting different selection pressures diverge populations into separate species.

questions.questionText: In the lac operon of E. coli, how does the presence of lactose turn structural transcription ON?

options.text: Allolactose binds to the repressor protein, changing its shape so it detaches from the operator

questions.explanation: Lactose acts as an inducer releasing the lac repressor so RNA polymerase transcribes β-galactosidase.

questions.questionText: In genetic engineering, which enzyme seals sugar-phosphate backbones by forming phosphodiester bonds between foreign DNA and a plasmid vector?
questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins sticky/blunt DNA ends via phosphodiester bonds to form recombinant DNA.

questions.questionText: Which plant hormone is produced at the coleoptile shoot tip and causes cell elongation on the shaded side during phototropism?
questions.explanation: IAA accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating acid-growth cell wall loosening and bending toward light.

questions.questionText: What happens inside sarcomeres when a skeletal muscle fibre contracts according to the sliding filament model?

options.text: Thin actin filaments slide over thick myosin filaments, shortening the I-band and H-zone while A-band stays constant
Myosin and actin filaments themselves shorten in length

questions.explanation: Filament lengths remain fixed while cross-bridges pull actin inward, narrowing H-zone and I-band.

questions.questionText: Which stage of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) occurs around 95°C?

options.text: DNA denaturation (separating double strands by breaking hydrogen bonds)

questions.explanation: Heating to ~95°C separates complementary DNA strands into single-stranded templates.

questions.questionText: In Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium (p² + 2pq + q² = 1), if 9% of a population shows a recessive condition (q² = 0.09), what percentage are heterozygous carriers (2pq)?
Which mode of natural selection favours intermediate birth weights in humans while selecting against very small and very large extremes?
questions.explanation: Stabilising selection reduces variance by preserving average phenotypes.

questions.questionText: In phloem translocation (pressure-flow hypothesis), how is sucrose loaded from leaf mesophyll into sieve-tube companion cells?
questions.explanation: Companion cells actively pump H⁺ out via ATP, driving sucrose inward through co-transporter proteins.

questions.questionText: Which bond stabilises the primary α-helix and β-pleated sheet secondary structures of proteins?

options.text: Hydrogen bonds between C=O and N-H backbone groups

questions.explanation: Regular backbone H-bonds between peptide groups stabilise α-helices and β-sheets.

questions.questionText: In ELISA and monoclonal antibody diagnostics, why are monoclonal antibodies highly specific?

options.text: They bind randomly to any carbohydrate
They are antibiotics produced by fungi
All antibodies come from one cloned plasma-cell hybridoma specific to a single antigen epitope

questions.explanation: Hybridoma clones yield pure identical antibodies binding one complementary antigen site.

questions.questionText: What is the net ATP gain directly produced by substrate-level phosphorylation from 1 molecule of glucose during glycolysis?
questions.explanation: Glycolysis invests 2 ATP and makes 4 ATP, yielding 2 net ATP (+ 2 NADH + 2 pyruvate).

questions.questionText: Which conservation approach breeds endangered black rhinos or wild dogs inside protected zoos/parks while frozen sperm/seed banks safeguard genetic diversity?
questions.explanation: Botanic gardens, seed vaults, and captive breeding outside natural habitats are ex situ conservation.

questions.questionText: Why is the C₄ photosynthetic pathway (e.g., maize and sugarcane in warm Zimbabwe) more efficient than C₃ crops (wheat/rice) in hot bright climates?

options.text: Spatial separation in bundle-sheath cells concentrates CO₂ around Rubisco, minimising wasteful photorespiration
C₄ plants do not need chlorophyll

questions.explanation: PEP carboxylase binds CO₂ strongly without binding O₂, raising bundle-sheath [CO₂] and suppressing photorespiration.
